_meta.name: QI Gate — public access policy
_meta.description: Single source of truth for what the internet may reach. Every Cloudflare tunnel points at Caddy on gate.listen_port; Caddy asks QI Gate whether the caller is logged in before proxying to the app.

_modes.protected: Login required for every path. Default for anything with a UI.
_modes.mixed: Login required EXCEPT the paths listed in public_paths (machine callbacks that authenticate themselves by signature).
_modes.open: No gate. Only for endpoints that carry their own strong auth, or that we have not yet finished verifying — each one must carry a 'why' and be revisited.

hosts.note: Crown jewels: ecosystem snapshot, service control, Brain data, war room. Was fully readable by anyone before 2026-08-05.
MapSnap has its own login (Application/auth.py) — the gate is a second wall in front of it. /mcp carries its own bearer token for the QI MCP Gateway, so it bypasses the cookie wall.
127.0.0.1 not localhost — M2V Gradio binds IPv4 only.
Separate registrable domain -> its own cookie, so it needs its own login. This host is the one the /wp-admin and /.env scanners were hitting.
Platform callbacks must stay reachable and verify their own signatures. Everything else on :8001 -- /panel, /memory, /history, /export, /admin/* -- was publicly readable and is now behind the gate.

hosts.why: Already enforces its own auth: bearer token for Claude Code, capability URL for claude.ai (qi_mcp_gateway.py). A cookie wall would break the MCP client, which cannot log in through a browser.
